Crimea Is Ukraine - United States Department of State

content.text:
**Legally, under international law and the position of most countries, Crimea is part of Ukraine, not Russia.** The UN General Assembly affirmed Ukraine’s territorial integrity in 2014 and called on states not to recognize changes to Crimea’s status after Russia’s annexation. ([press.un.org](https://press.un.org/en/2014/ga11493.doc.htm?utm_source=openai))

**In practice, Russia has controlled Crimea since 2014** after occupying and annexing it, and Russia treats it as part of the Russian Federation. Ukraine, the United States, the EU, and most of the international community regard Crimea as **Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory** and do not recognize the annexation. ([2021-2025.state.gov](https://2021-2025.state.gov/crimea-is-ukraine/?utm_source=openai))

So the short answer is: **Russia controls Crimea, but Crimea is internationally recognized by most states as Ukrainian territory.**
